transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-01-19
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Thompson (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (CTO, Vela), Aisha Malik (Lead ML Eng), Carlos Reyes (Infra), Priya Nair (PM)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be noisy):
Vela Payments is evaluating Redwood hosted + dedicated options. Primary integration concerns: SDK support, LangChain / LlamaIndex compatibility, routing through an internal gateway/proxy, rate limiting and quota enforcement, and observability hooks. Security questions: SOC2, KMS, VPC/private deployment. Next steps: pricing, dedicated demo, telemetry share, security docs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Thompson: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Can you hear me all right?
[00:05] Jordan Lee: Yep, loud and clear. Thanks.
[00:07] Maya Thompson: Awesome. Quick intros  I'm Maya, I'm the AE, Samir here is our SE. Samir, you wanna say hi?
[00:12] Samir Patel: Hey team, Samir Patel, I'm on the runtime infra side  happy to dig into latency, batching, quant profiles, all that.
[00:20] Jordan Lee: Jordan here, CTO. Aisha is our ML lead, Carlos handles infra and networking, Priya is PM.
[00:25] Aisha Malik: Hi all.
[00:27] Carlos Reyes: Hey.
[00:30] Maya Thompson: Great. The main goal today is to understand your integration points and constraints  SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex usage, how you want to route through your gateway, and what observability hooks you need. Is that accurate?
[00:38] Priya Nair: Yep, that covers it. We'll also want to understand pricing and what a pilot would look like.
[00:42] Maya Thompson: Perfect. Jordan, can you give a high level of your current stack and how you're planning to call models?
[00:47] Jordan Lee: Sure. We run a Node/Go backend; our customer flows generate prompts server-side, and we use a mix of synchronous and streaming responses for chat and fraud-detection heuristics. We're standardizing on a LangChain-ish orchestration  lots of chains and retrievers via LlamaIndex for RAG. We need low latency on the fraud paths, not as strict on the onboarding flows.
[01:10] Samir Patel: When you say low latency, ballpark p99 you're targeting?
[01:14] Jordan Lee: For fraud decisions we need p99 < 300ms ideally, p95 under 150ms would be great. For async flows we can tolerate seconds.
[01:22] Samir Patel: Okay. That informs whether dedicated GPU pools or hosted variants make sense.
[01:26] Aisha Malik: Also worth noting our request size: live fraud checks are usually short prompts, 200-600 tokens; some RAG retrievals can hit 1k-2k tokens. Volume spikes can be 600 rps for a few minutes during peak.
[01:40] Carlos Reyes: And we plan to route through our API gateway  we don't want to expose vendor credentials from our backend. We prefer a proxy/gateway pattern where our services call an internal gateway which then calls Redwood.
[01:52] Samir Patel: Totally common pattern. Redwood supports that  you can call our hosted API from your gateway, or we can deploy a private ingress in your VPC for Private deployments. If you want to preserve customer's IP and network controls we also support VPC peering and private endpoints.
[02:07] Jordan Lee: For the LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors  do you have maintained SDKs or adapters? We prefer minimal custom glue.
[02:15] Maya Thompson: We have official SDKs in Python and Node, and community adapters for LangChain + LlamaIndex. Samir, want to mention the LangChain connector status?
[02:22] Samir Patel: Yeah  we provide a first-class LangChain adapter with streaming support and function/tool calling. For LlamaIndex there's a maintained connector, but note sometimes the adapter names get munged in the transpilers  you might see older examples referencing 'RedwoodClient' vs 'redwood_sdk'. We'll send the latest code samples.
[02:39] Aisha Malik: That's good. Our stacks are mostly Python, but some microservices are Go. Is Go SDK feature-complete?
[02:46] Samir Patel: Go SDK exists and supports text/completions, embeddings, and streaming. A couple of advanced features like automatic prompt caching are better in Python currently but roadmap for parity.
[02:56] Priya Nair: On quotas and rate-limits  we have per-tenant quotas and throttles. Can you enforce fine-grained quotas per API key and per-route?
[03:06] Maya Thompson: Yes. For hosted we offer API key scoped limits and per-route rate-limiting configs. For Dedicated and Private you get more control  you can apply proxy-level limits in your gateway or use Redwood's quota API. There's a policy layer that can be configured, and we can also surface metrics for enforcement.
[03:23] Carlos Reyes: Do you support JWT-based auth from our gateway to Redwood so we don't leak raw keys? We rotate keys frequently.
[03:29] Samir Patel: You can use short-lived tokens via our token-exchange flow; for Private we also support mutual TLS and private endpoints. For Hosted, short-lived tokens via your gateway is the recommended pattern.
[03:40] Jordan Lee: Observability  we need tracing and token-level cost breakdowns. Can you plug into our Datadog / Honeycomb?
[03:47] Maya Thompson: Yes  we have outbound hooks and logs you can ship, plus direct integrations. We can emit OTLP traces and structured logs. For hosted customers, we expose per-request metadata including prompt size, model version, latency, token counts. For Dedicated, you get more retention and access to raw traces.
[04:04] Aisha Malik: Are there SDK-level hooks for streaming partial tokens to our consumers and for cancelling generation mid-stream?
[04:10] Samir Patel: Streaming is supported in both Node/Python. Cancellation mid-stream is supported via a cancel endpoint; behavior depends on the model runtime  we can implement best-effort cancellation. There's also prefix/KV cache controls to reduce repeated compute.
[04:23] Jordan Lee: You mentioned KV cache  does that interact with LangChain retrievers? We use LlamaIndex's index + cache, but want to avoid repeated tokenization cost.
[04:33] Samir Patel: KV cache is per-inference and stored in the serving layer to speed up autoregressive workloads. It doesn't directly replace retriever caches; you can use both. For RAG flows we'd recommend combining a retriever (LlamaIndex) and Redwood's prefix/KV caching to reduce repeated context compute. There might be some naming confusion in docs  sometimes people call it K-V cash or K-V cache, doc has been updated but please expect variation in older examples.
[04:54] Priya Nair: About data residency and encryption: we need KMS integration and customer-managed keys for Private. For Hosted, do you offer CMEK?
[05:03] Maya Thompson: For Hosted we do offer envelope encryption and integrations with major KMS providers for certain enterprise tiers; Dedicated and Private support customer-managed keys and HSM options. We'll attach the security pack with exact capabilities.
[05:16] Carlos Reyes: For Private deployment, what's the recommended network topology? We run in GCP  VPC peering or Private Service Connect?
[05:23] Samir Patel: Both are supported. We typically recommend a private endpoint inside your VPC with a small control plane egress for billing/telemetry. For on-prem air-gapped setups we ship an appliance package. We'll include topology diagrams.
[05:36] Jordan Lee: Pricing  rough numbers? We want to compare hosted per-token vs reserved capacity for dedicated GPUs.
[05:42] Maya Thompson: I'll send a tailored pricing sheet. High level: hosted is usage-based; dedicated is a reserved pool with commit and lower per-token cost at scale. We'll include sample math based on your throughput numbers.
[05:55] Aisha Malik: We do heavy embedding calls too  400k embeddings per day at times; do you have batching for embeddings?
[06:03] Samir Patel: Yes, embeddings batching is supported; and we expose batch size tuning. We also have a pre-batch queue to optimize GPU utilization. For Dedicated you can set max batch size and concurrency knobs.
[06:15] Priya Nair: On reliability  do you offer fallbacks between hosted and cheaper model variants if capacity is constrained?
[06:22] Maya Thompson: Yes  we have smart routing and automatic fallback policies; we can route by latency or cost. For critical fraud flows we recommend pinned dedicated capacity with failover to hosted reserved pool.
[06:35] Jordan Lee: Can you route specific routes to dedicated and others to hosted?
[06:38] Samir Patel: Absolutely  route by route pinning is supported. You can use tags or route IDs; we'll show config examples.
[06:46] Carlos Reyes: We're concerned about per-tenant isolation on Dedicated. Is tenant isolation handled by model sandboxing or infra-level?
[06:54] Samir Patel: Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools and process-level isolation. For strict regulatory needs we'd recommend Private where you control the entire infra. We'll share the dedicated isolation whitepaper.
[07:05] Jordan Lee: Aisha  any other integration quirks we should call out?
[07:08] Aisha Malik: We sometimes rely on function/tool calling and structured outputs (JSON) to avoid parsing. How reliable are the structured outputs and do you support function calling semantics like OpenAI?
[07:19] Maya Thompson: We support structured output and function/tool calling primitives. We also have output validators to enforce schema which you can plug into the SDK. It's not perfect  sometimes models hallucinate fields  but we do offer tools to reduce drift and have monitoring on structured output regression.
[07:34] Priya Nair: About quotas again  can we set soft quotas with alerting and hard quotas that reject?
[07:40] Samir Patel: Yes, there's soft-warning thresholds and hard caps. You can wire alerts into your pager or ours. For Hosted we can surface events to a webhook, for Dedicated you get more direct control.
[07:51] Jordan Lee: On the SDK side, how does rate-limiting behave when behind a gateway? If we get 600 rps into our gateway, what happens when Redwood enforces per-key limits?
[07:59] Samir Patel: Best practice is token exchange at gateway and per-route sharding. Redwood will return standard HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header. We also support per-route throttling callbacks so your gateway can implement smoothing to avoid spikes.
[08:14] Carlos Reyes: Do you provide client libraries for implementing exponential backoff patterns or is that up to us?
[08:19] Maya Thompson: Our SDKs include helpers for retry/backoff and idempotency tokens. We'll also surface rate-limit headers so you can implement adaptive client-side throttling.
[08:31] Priya Nair: For observability we want request-level metadata in our traces  correlation IDs and token counts. Do you support passing through our trace IDs so they're on your logs?
[08:39] Samir Patel: Yes, pass X-Request-ID or traceparent and we will propagate that to logs/traces. For Dedicated/Private you can get raw trace access or stream OTLP to your collectors.
[08:51] Aisha Malik: Regarding LangChain  how do you handle streaming tokens into chains and callbacks in long-running chains?
[08:58] Samir Patel: Chains that rely on streaming are supported; our LangChain adapter exposes token-level callbacks. For long running chains we recommend splitting into smaller steps and caching intermediate results. Also watch out for token window limits on large context RAGs  we provide strategies like context windowing and chunked retrieval.
[09:19] Jordan Lee: Any limitations we should be aware of with LlamaIndex? Some of our older connectors assumed synchronous responses and block on retrieval.
[09:27] Maya Thompson: Some community examples are older. Our maintained connector has async-friendly patterns and examples for LlamaIndex streaming. We'll include a sample repo link.
[09:36] Priya Nair: Security review  can we get SOC2, ISO docs and a pen test report?
[09:41] Maya Thompson: Yes, we'll attach the security pack with SOC2, ISO, pen test summary and compliance contacts. For Private deployments we support full audit logging with customer-managed retention.
[09:53] Carlos Reyes: We also need audit logs for admin actions and user-level access in the console. Does Redwood provide RBAC and SSO?
[09:59] Maya Thompson: Yes, RBAC and SSO (SAML / OIDC) are supported. For Hosted enterprise tiers we enforce SSO and can sync SCIM. Dedicated/Private allow more custom RBAC mappings.
[10:10] Jordan Lee: Onboarding  what's a minimal pilot look like if we wanted to validate latency and correctness?
[10:15] Maya Thompson: Typical pilot: 2-3 endpoints, one pinned to Dedicated for fraud path, one hosted for onboarding flows, a small dataset of prompts + evals, and a 2-week window to run traffic replay. We can run side-by-side benchmarks with your telemetry.
[10:29] Aisha Malik: For the evals, can Redwood run automatic regression checks against our golden prompt set?
[10:35] Samir Patel: Yes, Redwood Optimize can run prompt-set based regressions and send alerts when quality deviates. We'll propose a configuration for your test harness.
[10:45] Priya Nair: Any gotchas on token accounting and streaming  we need to bill internal teams correctly.
[10:52] Maya Thompson: We provide token-level accounting and can break down cost per-route or per-API key. For streaming, tokens emitted are accounted the same way as non-streaming, but we'll include a cost breakdown for intermediate partial tokens.
[11:04] Jordan Lee: Latency  can you share p50/p95/p99 numbers for models on dedicated vs hosted?
[11:10] Samir Patel: We'll share our benchmark deck. Roughly: small models on dedicated GPU pool p95 ~40-80ms depending on sequence length; p99 for tuned infra ~100-300ms. Hosted latency is similar but depends on multi-tenant load; Dedicated is more predictable. We'll send the performance profiles.
[11:26] Aisha Malik: Do you support quantized model variants for lower cost latency tradeoffs?
[11:31] Samir Patel: Yes, we support quantized variants and kernel selection optimizations. For RAG and embeddings we recommend specific quant profiles; we'll include recommended model+quant combos.
[11:44] Priya Nair: What about model versioning and rollouts  can we pin a route to a model version and do canary?
[11:50] Maya Thompson: Yes  rollouts, canaries, A/B tests are supported through the Console. You can do percentage rollouts and automatic fallback on error/regression.
[11:59] Carlos Reyes: From infra perspective, what's the observability retention and can we export raw logs to GCS / S3?
[12:06] Samir Patel: Logs can be exported to S3/GCS and retained per your plan for Dedicated/Private. Hosted has retention tiers. We'll include the export docs and retention SLAs.
[12:16] Jordan Lee: Anything else on integration patterns?
[12:19] Maya Thompson: I want to highlight two recommended patterns: 1) Gateway-proxy: your gateway issues short-lived tokens to Redwood, does per-tenant sharding and smoothing; 2) Direct private endpoint for critical low-latency routes where traffic flows inside your VPC to reduce network hops.
[12:35] Aisha Malik: For the gateway pattern, is there sample middleware for Go/Node to handle token exchange and retries?
[12:42] Samir Patel: Yes  sample middleware and a reference repo. We'll share those links.
[12:48] Priya Nair: On legal / procurement  what's the lead time for Dedicated?
[12:52] Maya Thompson: Depends on procurement; typical lead time from contract to capacity is 4-8 weeks, shorter if you accept our standard terms. Private/on-prem air-gapped is longer.
[13:03] Carlos Reyes: For the pilot, what telemetry do you need from us?
[13:07] Samir Patel: Sample traffic profiles, prompt sets, expected concurrency, and any compliance constraints. Aisha's note on embeddings + RAG size helps.
[13:17] Jordan Lee: OK. Next steps and owners?
[13:20] Maya Thompson: I'll recap  Maya will send pricing and dedicated spec by Friday Jan 21, Samir will schedule a dedicated runtime deep-dive the week of Jan 25, Aisha to share telemetry samples by Jan 22, and we'll attach SOC2 and security pack. Anything to add?
[13:33] Aisha Malik: That sounds right. Also please include LangChain/LlamaIndex sample repo links.
[13:38] Maya Thompson: Will do.
[13:40] Jordan Lee: One last question  if we need SLOs for fraud decisions, do you offer SLO-backed SLAs for Dedicated?
[13:47] Samir Patel: Yes  Dedicated comes with SLA targets and we can discuss p99 latency SLOs in the contract.
[13:54] Priya Nair: Great, thanks everyone.
[13:56] Maya Thompson: Thanks all  we'll follow up with the doc bundle.
[14:00] Jordan Lee: Thanks.

Notes / noise: transcript contains occasional mishears (e.g., K-V cash vs KV cache, Langchain spelled in docs as "Lang Chain" in some examples). Action items captured above.

End of call.
